facts.text: In 1857, a great struggle took place in India which completely shook the British Government.
facts.quote: In 1857, a great struggle took place in India which completely shook the British Government.

facts.text: V.D.Savarkar considered the scope and background of the struggle of 1857 in his book 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'.
facts.quote: The scope of the struggle of 1857 and its background was taken into consideration by V.D.Savarkar in his book 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'.

facts.text: In 1770, there was a major famine in the Bengal province, but the British rulers were indifferent.
facts.quote: In 1770, there was major famine in the Bengal province. But the British rulers were indifferent and insensitive towards Indian people.

facts.text: From 1763 to 1857 the peasants of Bengal participated in the rebellion led by Sanyasi-Fakir.
facts.quote: From 1763 to 1857 the peasants of Bengal participated in the rebellion led by Sanyasi-Fakir.

facts.text: Umaji Naik organised the Ramoshis and the local youth to revolt against the British; they drew a declaration and inspired people in Pune, Satara, Ahmednagar, Solapur, Nasik, Bhor etc.
facts.quote: He organised the Ramoshis and the local youth to revolt against the British. They drew a declaration and appealed to fight against the British and overthrow the government. They inspired people in Pune, Satara, Ahmednagar, Solapur, Nasik, Bhor etc.

facts.text: In 1832, Umaji Naik was arrested and hanged to death in Pune.
facts.quote: In 1832, Umaji Naik was arrested and hanged to death in Pune.

facts.text: Tribes and forest communities, whose livelihood depended on forest resources, fought the British: Kolam area of Chota Nagpur, Gonds of Orissa, Santhals of Bihar.
facts.quote: Consequently, Bihar, Kolam area of Chota Nagpur, Gonds of Orissa, Santhals of Bihar fought against the British.

facts.text: The Gadkaris from Kolhapur and Fond-Sawant from Konkan also challenged the British.
facts.quote: The Gadkaris from Kolhapur and Fond-Sawant from Konkan also challenged the British.

facts.text: In Odisha, the standing army of various independent kings was known as 'Paika'; they were granted rent free lands and had to stand by the king's side in war.
facts.quote: The standing army of various independent kings were known as 'Paika'. Rent free lands were granted to them for cultivation by the king. ... they were supposed to stand by the king's side in case of eruption of war.

facts.text: In 1803, the English conquered Odisha and took over the hereditary rent free lands of the Paikas.
facts.quote: In 1803, the English conquered Odisha. They took over the hereditary rent free lands granted to the Paikas.

facts.text: A rise in salt price due to tax also made life miserable; this resulted in an armed rebellion of Paikas against the British in 1817.
facts.quote: common man's life had also become miserable because of rise in salt price due to tax imposed on it by the British. This resulted in an armed rebellion of Paikas against the British in 1817.

facts.text: Bakshi Jaganbandhu Bidyadhar led the Paika revolt.
facts.quote: Bakshi Jaganbandhu Bidyadhar led this revolt.

facts.text: In 1806 at Vellore the revolt of Indian sepoys took up a fierce form.
facts.quote: In 1806 at Vellore and in 1824 at Barrackpore the revolt took up a fierce form.

facts.text: In 1824 at Barrackpore the revolt of Indian sepoys took up a fierce form.
facts.quote: In 1806 at Vellore and in 1824 at Barrackpore the revolt took up a fierce form.

facts.text: The rebellions before 1857 were local in nature and single handed; the British forcibly broke them down.
facts.quote: They were local in nature and single handed. The British forcibly broke down the revolts.

facts.text: Economic causes: a new revenue system, taxes forcibly extracted from farmers, heavy taxes on local industries; the handicraft and textile industry of India were ruined.
facts.quote: The British introduced new revenue system to increase their income. Taxes were forcibly extracted from the farmers. ... They imposed heavy taxes on the local industries. The handicraft and textile industry of India were ruined.

facts.text: Social causes: Indians felt Sati prohibition and the widow remarriage act were interference in their lifestyle.
facts.quote: Sati prohibition, widow remarriage act were correct from social point of view, but the Indians thought that it is an interference in their lifestyle

facts.text: After 1757 the British took charge of many Indian states.
facts.quote: After 1757 the British took charge of many Indian states.

facts.text: Lord Dalhousie annexed many princely states; the Nawab of Ayodhya was dethroned on grounds of maladministration.
facts.quote: Later Lord Dalhousie annexed many princely states on various causes. The Nawab of Ayodhya was dethroned on grounds of maladministration

facts.text: The princely states of Satara, Nagpur and Jhansi were annexed through the doctrine of lapse.
facts.quote: the princely states of Satara, Nagpur and Jhansi were annexed through the doctrine of lapse.

facts.text: Indian soldiers could not gain any post higher than the Subhedar and were paid less than British soldiers.
facts.quote: They could not gain any post higher than the Subhedar. They were paid less compared to the British soldiers.

facts.text: Immediate cause: in 1856, the British provided long range enfield rifles to the Indian sepoys, who had to bite the end of the cartridges.
facts.quote: In 1856, the British provided long range enfield rifles to the Indian sepoys. The sepoys were required to bite the end of the cartridges.

facts.text: News spread that the cartridges were smeared in the fats of cow and pig, which hurt Hindu and Muslim sepoys.
facts.quote: The news spread out that these cartridges were smeared in the fats of cow and pig. Due to this the religious sentiments of Hindu and Muslim sepoys were hurt

facts.text: Mangal Pandey from Barrackpore cantonment shot an English officer; he was arrested and hanged to death.
facts.quote: Mangal Pandey from Barrackpore cantonment shot an English officer as a reaction to unjust nature of British officers. Mangal Pandey was arrested and hanged to death.

facts.text: The entire regiment of Indian sepoys at Meerut took part in the struggle and marched towards Delhi.
facts.quote: The entire regiment of Indian sepoys at Meerut took part in the freedom struggle and marched towards Delhi.

facts.text: The sepoys handed over the leadership to Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah and proclaimed him the Emperor of India.
facts.quote: They handed over the leadership of the freedom struggle to Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah and proclaimed him as the Emperor of India.

facts.text: The revolt spread in cantonments from Bihar to Rajputana and in Lucknow, Allahabad, Kanpur, Banaras, Bareli and Jhansi; later it spread to South India.
facts.quote: The Indian soldiers revolted in cantonments from Bihar to Rajputana. The revolt spread in Lucknow, Allahabad, Kanpur, Banaras, Bareli, and Jhansi. Later it spread to South India.

facts.text: Chhatrapati Pratapsingh of Satara and his officer Rango Bapuji, Chimasaheb of Kolhapur, Babasaheb Bhave of Nargund and Bhagoji Naik of Ahmednagar were in the forefront.
facts.quote: In the revolt, Chhatrapati Pratapsingh of Satara and his officer Rango Bapuji, Chimasaheb of Kolhapur, Babasaheb Bhave of Nargund, Bhagoji Naik of Ahmednagar were in the forefront.

facts.text: The Royal queen of Peth, Surgana from Nasik district also participated in the struggle.
facts.quote: Royal queen of Peth, Surgana from Nasik district also participated in the struggle.

facts.text: In 1857, under the leadership of Kajarsingh, the Bhills revolted, whereas Shankarshah led the revolt in Satpura region.
facts.quote: In 1857, under the leadership of Kajarsingh, the Bhills revolted, whereas Shankarshah led the revolt in Satpura region.

facts.text: 400 Bhill women participated in the revolt at Khandesh.
facts.quote: 400 Bhill women participated in the revolt at Khandesh.

facts.text: In the 18th century, after the weakening of the Mughal Empire, invaders like Nadirshah and Abdali attacked India; the Marathas fought Abdali at Panipat.
facts.quote: after the weakening of Mughal Empire, invaders like Nadirshah, Abdali attacked India. ... The Marathas fought against Abdali at Panipat for the same reason.

facts.text: As Bahadur Shah was incapable of fighting, Nanasaheb Peshwa, Rani Laxmibai of Jhansi and Tatya Tope took up the charge of the struggle.
facts.quote: the descendant of Mughals, Bahadur Shah, was incapable of fighting against the British. Understanding the condition, Nanasaheb Peshwa, Rani Laxmibai of Jhansi and Tatya Tope took up the charge of the freedom struggle of 1857.

facts.text: Maulavi Ahmed Allah, Kunwar Singh, Mughal commander Bakht Khan and Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in various regions.
facts.quote: Maulavi Ahmed Allah, Kunwar Singh, Mughal commander Bakht Khan, Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in various regions.

facts.text: The nature of revolt in Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi and West Bihar was more fierce.
facts.quote: The nature of revolt in Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, West Bihar was more fierce.

facts.text: The Indian sepoys started the freedom struggle before the fixed time.
facts.quote: The Indian sepoys started the freedom struggle before the fixed time.

facts.text: Within the next six months the British regained the lost territories; Rani Laxmibai, Kunwar Singh and Ahmedullah laid their lives.
facts.quote: The British made quick recovery and within next six months regained the lost territories. Rani Laxmibai, Kunwar Singh, Ahmedullah laid their lives.

facts.text: Bahadur Shah was imprisoned at Rangoon.
facts.quote: Bahadur Shah was imprisoned at Rangoon.

facts.text: Nanasaheb and Begum Hazrat Mahal took shelter in Nepal.
facts.quote: Nanasaheb and Begum Hazrat Mahal took shelter in Nepal

facts.text: Tatya Tope fought for the next ten months, but due to betrayal he was caught and hanged to death.
facts.quote: Tatya Tope fought for next ten months against the British but due to betrayal he was caught and hanged to death.

facts.text: By the end of 1858, the British ruthlessly crushed down the struggle.
facts.quote: In this way, by the end of 1858, the British ruthlessly crushed down the struggle.

facts.text: Peasants, artisans, common people and tribes joined; Hindus and Muslims stood up together with the aim of overthrowing the British, so the struggle gained a national form.
facts.quote: In this rebellion, Hindus, Muslims stood up with a great force. Their common aim was overthrowing the British from India. ... therefore this freedom struggle gained a national form.

facts.text: Cause of failure: the struggle was not comprehensive; it was more severe in North India, but Rajputana, Punjab, some parts of Bengal and North west India remained aloof.
facts.quote: Its intensity was more severe in North India, but Rajputana, Punjab, some parts of Bengal and North west India remained aloof.

facts.text: Cause of failure: lack of central leadership - there was no commonly accepted leader.
facts.quote: There was no commonly accepted leader to fight against the British.

facts.text: Cause of failure: most of the feudatory princes remained aloof; except a few, they remained faithful to the British.
facts.quote: But except a few others remained faithful to the British.

facts.text: Cause of failure: lack of military tactics; the rebels captured Delhi but could not retain it and had limited armed supply.
facts.quote: They captured Delhi but could not retain it. Similarly, the Indian rebels had limited armed supply.

facts.text: The international situation favoured the British: the Crimean war with Russia was just over and the British won it; their naval strength was vast.
facts.quote: The Crimean war with Russia was just over. The British won the war. ... The naval strength of British was vast.

facts.text: The British Parliament ended the rule of the Company and took over ruling India through the Government of India Act 1858.
facts.quote: It forced the British Parliament to end the rule of the Company and instead take over the responsibility of ruling over the people of India through the Government of India Act 1858.

facts.text: The Governor General was now designated as the Viceroy of India; Lord Canning was the last Governor General and the first Viceroy of India.
facts.quote: The Governor General was now designated as the Viceroy of India. Lord Canning happened to be the last Governor General and the first Viceroy of India.

facts.text: A new post called Secretary of State was created in the British Government to look after the affairs of India.
facts.quote: A new post called Secretary of State was created in the British Government to look after the affairs of India.

facts.text: Queen Victoria's Proclamation: no discrimination on race, religion, caste or birth place; government services on merit; no interference in religious affairs; no princely state annexed henceforth.
facts.quote: Queen Victoria of England issued a Declaration addressing the people of India. ... Government services will be given on merit. There will be no interference in religious affairs. ... no princely state will be annexed henceforth.

facts.text: Army changes: the proportion of British soldiers was increased, artillery was kept exclusively with the British and the military was divided on basis of caste.
facts.quote: The proportion of British soldiers was increased in the army. ... Artillery was kept exclusively in the hands of the British. There was division of military on basis of caste.

facts.text: The British accepted non interference in social and religious aspects and adopted the 'Divide and Rule policy'.
facts.quote: The British accepted the policy of non interference in social and religious aspects of Indians. ... They adopted the policy of polluting the minds of Indians by following the 'Divide and Rule policy'.

facts.text: The freedom struggle of 1857 became an inspiration of the Indian freedom movement.
facts.quote: The freedom struggle of 1857 became an inspiration of Indian freedom movement.
